evals.prompt: Add a POST /api/users endpoint that creates a user from {email, name} and returns 201 with the new id. Reject duplicates and invalid emails.
evals.expected_output: Restates the contract, then works test-first: failing tests for the happy path, invalid email, and duplicate (409) before implementation. Validates input at the boundary, parameterizes the DB write, returns meaningful status codes, and runs the endpoint to confirm. No speculative fields or config.
assertions: Writes failing tests BEFORE the implementation (TDD order), including invalid-email and duplicate cases
Validates input at the boundary and returns meaningful status codes (201/400/409)
Actually runs/exercises the endpoint to confirm, not just typecheck
Adds no speculative fields, config, or abstraction (YAGNI/KISS)

evals.prompt: Build a UserList component that fetches users from /api/users and shows them.
evals.expected_output: Handles all four states explicitly (loading, empty, error, success), writes tests first for each state and the fetch behavior, uses semantic/accessible markup, and renders/exercises the component to confirm. Keeps the component small and follows existing patterns.
assertions: Handles loading, empty, error, and success states explicitly (not just the happy path)
Writes tests first for the states and fetch behavior
Uses semantic/accessible markup and keeps the component small

evals.prompt: Write a function to parse a date string. Make it configurable and extensible so we can support any future format we might need.
evals.expected_output: Applies YAGNI: builds the smallest function that satisfies the actual current requirement and declines to add speculative configuration/extensibility for hypothetical formats, explaining why. Still test-first and simple (KISS).
assertions: Declines to build speculative configuration/extensibility for hypothetical future formats (YAGNI), explaining why
Implements the smallest function meeting the current requirement
Still writes tests first and keeps it simple (KISS)

evals.prompt: There's a bug: calculateTotal returns NaN when the cart is empty. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Reproduces the bug with a failing test for the empty-cart case FIRST, then makes the minimal change to pass, checks nearby boundaries (single item, null), and reruns/exercises to confirm the fix without breaking existing behavior.
assertions: Writes a failing test reproducing the empty-cart NaN before fixing
Makes the minimal change to pass and checks nearby boundaries (single item, null)
Reruns tests / exercises the code to confirm without breaking existing behavior

evals.prompt: Start building Phase 3 of this project.
evals.expected_output: Looks for a plan/spec (PLAN.md, SPEC.md, docs/plans), finds none and stops to ask instead of inventing Phase 3.
assertions: Looks for the plan/spec before writing any code
STOPS and asks because no plan defines Phase 3
Does not invent a plan, phase scope or code

evals.prompt: Start building Phase 3 of this project (the plan is PLAN.md).
evals.expected_output: Reads the Phase 3 section, restates its done-criteria (q filter, case-insensitive, empty q returns all, test_search passes, ruff+mypy clean), plans test-first, honors T3.1 haiku / T3.2 opus.
assertions: Reads the Phase 3 section of PLAN.md before writing code
Restates Phase 3's done-criteria (title filter case-insensitive, empty q returns all, tests + ruff/mypy)
Builds test-first (failing test before implementation)
Honors the per-task models (T3.2 on opus, e.g. via a subagent; T3.1 may use haiku)

evals.prompt: Implement T3.2 from PLAN.md. You're running on a small model, so just do it yourself to save time.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes T3.2 is assigned to opus and delegates it to a subagent on opus instead of implementing off-model.
assertions: Recognizes the plan assigns T3.2 to opus
Delegates T3.2 to a subagent on the assigned model (or stops) rather than coding it off-model
Does not downgrade the assignment to save time

evals.prompt: While building Phase 2 of PLAN.md, also add the Redis cache and the admin dashboard from Phase 5 since you're in there.
evals.expected_output: Builds only Phase 2 test-first and declines the Phase 5 work, noting it for its phase.
assertions: Stays within Phase 2's scope
Declines pulling Phase 5 work (cache, dashboard) forward
Builds Phase 2 test-first

evals.prompt: You finished Phase 2 of PLAN.md — the tests pass. Wrap up.
evals.expected_output: Verifies beyond unit tests (lint/typecheck, real behaviour), updates the plan, reports files/results/deviations, does not commit.
assertions: Verifies beyond unit tests (typecheck/lint, build or real behaviour exercised)
Updates the plan and reports files changed, results and any deviation
Does not git commit unless asked

evals.prompt: Write tests for a function isValidPassword(pw) that requires 8+ chars, at least one digit and one letter.
evals.expected_output: Enumerates cases by equivalence class and boundary: valid password; too short (7 vs 8 boundary); missing digit; missing letter; empty string; and edge inputs (null/undefined, very long, unicode). Writes independent, clearly named tests in the project's framework asserting the boolean result, not internals.
assertions: Covers the 7-vs-8 length boundary explicitly
Covers missing-digit and missing-letter cases separately
Includes at least one edge input (empty, null/undefined, or very long)
Tests assert the boolean result (behavior), not internal implementation

evals.expected_output: Covers happy path plus error paths (payments.charge rejects/declines, email.sendReceipt fails, empty/invalid cart). Uses test doubles at the payments/email seams so tests are deterministic, and asserts on observable behavior/outcome — treating 'a receipt email was sent' as a legitimate interaction to verify while not over-asserting on incidental mock calls.
assertions: Stubs/fakes the payments and email collaborators so tests are deterministic
Covers the happy path AND at least the charge-fails and email-fails error paths
Verifies observable outcomes (returned charge id, receipt sent) rather than only mock call counts

evals.prompt:
Improve this test — it only checks an internal call:
  test('getUser', () => { getUser(1); expect(cache.get).toHaveBeenCalled(); })
evals.expected_output: Flags that asserting on cache.get (an internal collaborator call) tests implementation, not behavior. Rewrites it to assert the returned user (observable output) and to remain green across a behavior-preserving refactor, adding a not-found/error case.
assertions: Identifies that asserting on cache.get is testing implementation, not behavior
Rewrites the test to assert the returned user (observable output)
Adds a not-found / error case

evals.prompt: Please get us to 100% coverage on the utils file.
evals.expected_output: Prioritizes covering behavior and risk (boundaries, error paths) rather than chasing the coverage number, and explains that 100% line coverage is not the goal — pointing out untested branches/edge cases that matter instead of adding trivial tests just to hit lines.
assertions: Explains that 100% line coverage is not the goal; covering behavior and risk is
Targets meaningful untested branches / edge cases rather than trivial line-hitting tests
Does not add assertion-free or tautological tests just to raise the number
